info.desc: 21 is the second studio album by English singer-songwriter Adele. It was released on 24 January 2011 in Europe and on 22 February 2011 in North America by XL Recordings and Columbia Records. The album was named after the age of the singer during its production. 21 shares the folk and Motown soul influences of her 2008 debut album 19, but was further inspired by the American country and Southern blues music to which she had been exposed during her 2008–09 North American tour An Evening with Adele. Composed in the aftermath of the singer's separation from her then partner, .

podcast.body: Adele's album "21" had established her as "one of the biggest selling artists in the universe" by 2012 when the producers of the James Bond film "Skyfall" approached her for the theme song. Her immense success at the time made her a prime candidate for the high-profile commission. "Adele was one of the biggest selling artists in the universe with her 21 album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Adele's second album, "21," was initially withheld from digital platforms, including Spotify and almost YouTube, as she became a significant opponent of these services. She eventually relented, making the album available digitally. "se negaba sacar su segundo trabajo, trabajo del 21, en las plataformas digitales. Casi estincluyendo YouTube. Al final se acababa rindiendo y se acababa rindiendo y acabándolo."

podcast.body: This album by Adele swept the Grammy Awards in 2012, being described as "more acclaimed and even better selling" than her later Album of the Year winner, "25." "She'd already swept the awards in 2012 for her more acclaimed and even better selling 21 album."

podcast.body: This album, released in 2011, was a blockbuster success and was filled with songs of heartbreak. It established Adele's command of the year, similar to The Beatles in 1964. "The year she released her blockbuster album, 21, on an LP filled with songs of heartbreak, rolling in the deep, stood out."
